data.reason: The KPI names the town-wide count of orders delivered within the promised times as the objective, so on_time_deliveries should be the primary metric. Options 1 and 2 both do this; option 3 does not. The KPI also allows the promised times to be revised, but it requires that any change worse for customers be justified by measuring its effect on them. late_deliveries, which option 2 monitors, is defined against the same promise as on_time_deliveries. A looser promise would therefore look better on every goal in option 2 even if customers waited longer. Option 1 adds p95_wait_s, max_wait_s and unfinished, which do not depend on the promise. This gives the measurement on the same seeds that the KPI asks for before a contract change is accepted. I follow the LLM's recommendation. No numeric targets or guard values are set, because the KPI states none. Company-level fairness metrics are left out, because the KPI does not mention them.
assumptions: p95_wait_s and max_wait_s measure time from order to delivery and do not depend on the DELIVERY_SLA promise.
Measurements on the same random seeds make before/after comparisons of wait times valid across promise revisions.
Any DELIVERY_SLA revision will be sent to a human, with the measured wait and unfinished changes attached.
unknowns: The current baseline values of on_time_deliveries, p95_wait_s, max_wait_s and unfinished.
Whether the operator has an acceptable maximum customer wait in mind; none is stated.
Whether per-company on-time rates will diverge if only the town-wide total is optimized.
How much on-time count the operator would trade for longer waits; no exchange rate is defined.

predictions.subject: metric:on_time_deliveries
predictions.note: Rule proposals will be judged on this primary metric, so adopted changes should raise it.

predictions.subject: metric:unfinished
predictions.note: Choosing a reading does not change the simulation itself; this only changes once rules are amended.

predictions.subject: metric:p95_wait_s
predictions.note: This is monitored only. It should not worsen through rule changes alone.

follow_ups.text: Check whether the town-wide on-time gains are concentrated in one company. If min_company_on_time_rate drops noticeably, ask the human whether to add company-level metrics.
Once baseline wait values are measured, ask the operator whether a ceiling on p95_wait_s or max_wait_s should be set as a guard.
